checks.reason: Both conjuncts correctly encode that addRewards and claimRewards are external, perform transfers/state changes, and lack a nonReentrant guard.
The implication correctly states that when accounting is increased and transferFrom not completed, no reentrant entrypoint is invoked.
The predicate directly encodes that griefing is enabled by the reentrancy window.

piv_relation.reason: Report evidence explicitly states the unguarded addRewards/claimRewards reentrancy window enables griefing, supporting the P-to-I-to-V link.

evidence.text: Distributor.addRewards updates internal pending-reward accounting before performing the external transferFrom call. A malicious token can re-enter during transferFrom and call claimRewards (or other entrypoints) while accounting has already been increased, producing a clear reentrancy window that can be used for griefing and, in some scenarios, monetary extraction.

Attackers can force the code path to re-enter claimRewards during addRewards, demonstrating an exploitable reentrancy window. This enables griefing and may be combined with other weaknesses to steal tokens.

unresolved.description: Report does not establish whether the reentrant call to claimRewards or other entrypoints is authorized or succeeds; only the exposure of the window is stated.

limitations: The intent is encoded as absence of a reentrant entrypoint invocation during the window between pending-accounting increase and transferFrom completion; the report does not specify which entrypoints or authorization state apply.
Griefing is represented as a grounded Boolean because the report provides no more specific observable outcome.
